scope: The open-weight Decision Index 0.3.1 leaders plus the best small open entries and their base models: tier 1 (twelve repositories the next family effort should start from, including the whole d3 family) and tier 2 (the remaining board entries surveyed, several under non-commercial licenses). Supplemental research metadata, not a catalog: nothing installs from this file. Six entries (d3-edge, d3-lite, d3-nano, d3-mini, d3-flash, and sieve-4b) have since landed as catalog profiles that load their pinned weights; they set openkind_loadable and name their catalog_profile. Every other entry records the blocker that keeps OpenKind's loaders from accepting it today. Each entry pins the re-resolved revisions of the upstream weights and any MLX conversion leads so later qualification starts from immutable sources. Supersedes registry/v1/jev-decision-index.json (Decision Index 0.2.1), which is retained as history.

source.ranking_field_note: The Space's 0.3.1 Full score v = 0.20 public + 0.50 private same-skills + 0.30 private new-domains, equated onto the public scale; ties are declared inside a 0.9-point band, so the d3 and Decider 31B tie group is not separable. The 0.2.1 edition ranked on scores.balanced_skill instead. All three bundle files were fetched at the pinned Space revision on 2026-10-12 and hash-match the recorded digests.

pin_policy: Every revision was re-resolved against the Hub API on 2026-10-12; head_at_survey is the commit observed at the earlier survey and equivalent_revisions lists observed HEADs whose weight, readout, and config blobs are byte-identical (same sizes and LFS sha256) to the pin - only README, runtime server, or processor files moved. Where a board run or parity record evaluated a specific release commit, that commit is the pin even when tags point elsewhere (the d3 family's Hub tags v3.1.0/v3.1.1/v3.1.2 disagree with the semantic-router release pins). No weights were downloaded; all observations are Hub API metadata and shipped configs.

base_model.architecture: Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration hybrid: hidden 5120, 64 layers in a 3:1 linear:full pattern, DeltaNet 16 key / 48 value heads x 128 with conv kernel 4, GQA 24 query / 4 KV heads x 256, full_attention_interval 4, partial rotary 0.25 theta 1e7, vocab 248320 - the same architecture openkind implements, at exactly the clef-27B dims

weights.format: merged BF16 safetensors, 11 shards, 52,170,802,640 bytes, plus a separate 5,222,480-byte readout.safetensors ([255, 5120] float32 rows); decision_config.json declares format d3-code-readout-v1 version 1, attention_mode noncausal_full_attention, pooling last, temperature 1.0, and 255 answer codes mapped to token ids; Ships d3_format.py, d3_runtime.py, and d3_server.py implementing the d3-code-readout-v1 contract: tokenizer.encode the rendered prompt, one noncausal forward, softmax the 255 code logits at the last position at temperature 1.0, and map codes to answer tokens
weights.notes: The pin is the commit the Decision Index board run and the vLLM semantic-router parity record evaluated (the 'd3 v3.1.0' release commit; the Hub tag v3.1.0 points elsewhere). HEAD moved four times on 2026-10-12 over runtime server files only; every weight, readout, and config blob is byte-identical (same sizes and LFS sha256) between the pin and HEAD, so HEAD is recorded as equivalent. The Hub tag v3.1.1 and v3.1.2 exist and were not evaluated by the board.

entries.blocker: The qwen3_5 hybrid backbone kernels exist at these dims (the clef family), but the checkpoint needs what no openkind family has yet: the noncausal full-attention mask in the 16 full-attention layers (repeated_full execution only, no state forking), the separate 255-row float32 readout, the d3-code-readout-v1 prompt bytes, and the vision tower for image and video input.
entries.nearest_openkind_path: A d3 family adapter (noncausal mask + d3-code-readout-v1 readout) over the existing qwen3_5 27B-class backbone execution, with the vision path as a later increment; text-only entries of the same family are the practical first targets.

mlx_leads.notes: Unverified third-party conversion (2 shards, d3_mlx.py, readout.safetensors, decision_config.json; no license field). Never downloaded or compared against the source; not parity evidence.
Backbone-only conversion already pinned by the 0.2.1 file; carries no decision readout.

base_model.architecture: Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration dense text stack: hidden 5376, 60 layers in a 5:1 sliding:full pattern, sliding window 1024, 32 query / 16 KV heads plus 4 global KV heads, head_dim 256 / global 512, attention_k_eq_v true, no per-layer-input embeddings and no KV sharing, dual rope, final_logit_softcapping 30.0

weights.format: 4 NVFP4 safetensors shards, 32,633,477,808 bytes (about 31 GB with FP8 KV cache as served); no unquantized checkpoint exists in this repository; decider_config.json carries the two-reading rule (first reading at T1(n) = 2.042 + 0.003 ln n, second reversed-options reading below 0.7 confidence, re-normalized at T2(n) = 1.953 + 0.010 ln n)
weights.notes: The pin is the commit the card says produced its 64.27 public run. HEAD (e12ddf20) differs only in README.md; all four weight shards are byte-identical between pin and HEAD, so HEAD is recorded as equivalent.

entries.blocker: Three stacked blockers: NVFP4 weights and openkind has no NVFP4 execution path; the gemma4 family loader is fail-closed pinned to E4B geometry and rejects the dense 31B stack; and the two-reading rule is a per-question re-read with reversed options that changes the serving contract for Choice questions. The decider letter-slot readout contract itself is the one openkind already implements at 4B.
entries.nearest_openkind_path: Decider-family letter readout over a new gemma4 dense-31B backbone config once an NVFP4-capable or dequantized execution path exists; the two-reading rule would be a profile-level policy.

mlx_leads.notes: Backbone-only conversion already pinned by the 0.2.1 file; carries no decision readout.

entries.blocker: The enable_noncausal_full_attention hook lifts the causal mask in the 16 full-attention layers, which forces the repeated_full execution strategy and gives up state forking; the separate 255-row half-precision readout, the autojev record-style prompt, the 8,192-token cap, and the optional image path all need a new family adapter. The BF16 checkpoint is also about 49 GiB, above this project's 36 GB reference host.
entries.nearest_openkind_path: A pplx family adapter (noncausal mask + 255-row readout) over the existing qwen3_5 27B-class backbone execution; MLX 4-bit conversion exists but is unverified, so parity would start from the BF16 checkpoint on larger hardware.
